precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 33:10
precepts.why:
Genesis 2:7 says “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” People talk about evolution, that man came up from primates and formed over time into what we know today; that is not true. Everything in Israel United in Christ is done to edify the nation, and what we say we prove out of the word of God. Ecclesiasticus 33:10 is the second witness: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.”

Some will ask how we know man was made from the dust, since that is not what the white man’s science says. Science is only good if it goes with the Bible; if it contradicts the Bible, we don't give a damn about science. But the honest science agrees. The infographic From Dust to Dust, the elements that connect us to Earth, shows that the human body is made mainly of elements also found in soil. The six main elements of life, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur, are in every cell, molecule and structure of the body and make up over 99 percent of our mass. The essential minerals, calcium for bones and teeth, potassium for the muscles and heart, magnesium, sodium and chlorine, are the same nutrients the soil gives the plants. The trace elements, iron for carrying oxygen, zinc for the immune system and healing, silicon and manganese, are in the soil too. We come from the earth, and to the earth we return, just like the Bible says.

The Most High is a mastermind, the author of beauty, the creator of all things, and he knew what he was doing when he pulled Adam from the dust of the ground. Our bodies are a testament that his word is true. The Bible is a true book, and we don't give a damn what anybody has to say about how our God, our father, created us. The teaching that man came from primates is there to contradict God’s word, because they know our God is a black man.

Paul says the same: “The first man is of the earth, earthy,” and “As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy.” Adam was earthy, and so are we; we come from the same soil as our father Adam, and “as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.” Meanwhile the other nations make sure we are deficient in these very things, and much of the food we eat diminishes them to kill us faster. So it is important, brothers and sisters, to keep a healthy diet.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 2:5
precepts.why:
God told Noah, “Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.” Why was Noah chosen to be delivered with his family? Peter explains it: God “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”.

The old world is the world we read about in Genesis 7, and God did not spare it: he killed all flesh. Noah was righteous because he preached righteousness and kept the commandments. He was a godly man in an ungodly world, and he had received his orders from God on exactly how to build the ark and did it faithfully. His standing up for God is what brought the flood in upon the ungodly.

Why is he called the eighth person? The other seven were his wife, his three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their wives. Noah is counted eighth because a true captain, a true leader, made sure his wife, his sons and their wives were on first, and he was the last one to get on the ark. When Noah gave the word, they did not question him; they got on.

That is why men of God have to be strong. We come to the Sabbath because we are sick. We are surrounded by the world all week and fighting the sin around us and in our own thoughts, so we need to be around brothers and sisters who will correct us in righteousness.

The flood shows the mind of God for destruction. Nobody was righteous except the ones on the ark. The coming destruction, a thermonuclear war, will be on another level, and we want to be spiritually the men and women in that ark, not the ones drowning. A lot more than eight will make it this time, but very few, so do not be surprised when your family does not listen. Keep the commandments, preach righteousness, and God will deliver us.

precepts.label: Proverbs 3:1-5
precepts.why:
“The Lord is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God”. He will guide us. Many of us choose the ways of the world to guide us: the job guides you, the children guide you. But each of us has to walk a path, some of us start to go off it, and we have to seek good and not evil. Proverbs 3 shows what his guiding looks like.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments”. Whose law? God's laws. Your heart is your mind. You have to learn the laws and keep the commandments, and that proves the laws are the commandments. “For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee”. You want to live long? Despite all these wars, rumors of wars and mayhem throughout the world, you want peace? Do what he said.

“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding”. Trust that the prophecies have to go in order. Iran is not going to bring in World War III; Iran will help unite the Arabs, and you are seeing it. And lean not on your own understanding: in the Christian church some of us used to say we're already saved. No, that's not the understanding. He that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved, and we don't know when that end is coming. So we keep enduring, keeping the commandments, seeking the good and not the evil. “In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths”.

That is how the Lord becomes our salvation in Exodus 15:2: trust in him, endure to the end, and do his commandments. Then the habitation we prepare him is the kingdom, where we have power and rule and every wrong done to us is turned upside down, not the pie-in-the-sky fairy tale of modern Christianity. The Lord is a man of war, and he is using these nations to bring a final battle. I pray I make it, and I pray you make it.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:32
precepts.why:
“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”: in chattel slavery our lives were in doubt every day. Every day there was a chance we would be killed, a chance we might get lynched. And not only the lives of the mothers and fathers were in doubt; our sons were in doubt too. That is why verse 32 is read here: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people.”

That could have happened at any moment, any day. Your son ripped out of your arms to be sold to Master so-and-so, and you would never see your children again. From the day that child was born until the day someone said, I want that one as a slave, the parents lived with it, and they had nothing to say about it. “and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long”: they watched their sons get taken away and watched their daughters get taken away. That is the failing of eyes and the sorrow of mind of verse 65: no way to change your reality, no future you can see for your children.

“and there shall be no might in thine hand”: no might in our hands to stop it. And there was no alcohol for them. A bottle of whiskey would not have stopped that. They had to endure this thing sober, knowing the Lord was still going to be with us somehow, some way. So they could not off themselves, because a generation was going to come from them, from the wife and from the husband, and our seed would continue while they went through trauma after trauma.

It took faith to make it from morning to night and night to morning, and they did not even have the truth the way we know it today. They pushed through all that evil and ugliness so that you and I could sit here today. So what excuse do we have? We cannot leave our post to drink and get high, or put our head inside a bottle and a crack pipe, when our forefathers endured this and kept pushing.

precepts.label: John 3:3
precepts.why:
A lot of us are not finding comfort in the scriptures because we lack faith. You don’t believe the Bible can transform you. You don’t believe it can turn you into another man, that you could become a whole different person. But 1 Samuel 10:6 says it: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

John 3:3 says the same thing to Nicodemus: “Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

Being turned into another man is being born again. The brother who drank a whole fifth in one night, the one who says, I can’t put it down, it’s a part of me, is not stuck being that man. Except he be born again, turned into another man, he cannot see the kingdom. The bottle is the battle, and the Bible is how you are turned into another man and win it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:34

1 Samuel 10:6 says you “shalt be turned into another man.” 2 Esdras 14:34 tells you what your part is in that turning.

“Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.”

Subdue your own understanding and reform your heart. We have to be transformed in the renewing of our minds. Transformed.

That is what the brother with the addiction runs from. He comes to the table having drunk a whole fifth in one night and says he is not an alcoholic. Even the white man knows the first step of recovery is to admit it: you have to realize you need help, that you are sick. Has he watched the classes on alcohol the Bishops and Deacons go over all the time? No. Why not? Because he is running away from his issues, and you cannot run away from that thing. You have to subdue your own understanding, reform your heart, and let the word turn you into another man, and then you shall be kept alive and after death obtain mercy.

precepts.label: Matthew 11:28
precepts.why:
The bottle says, forget your pain; the Bible says, “Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee.” The bottle says, numb your sorrow. Christ answers that lie: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”

The bottle offers to carry your burden for you. It talks to you like scripture in a dark room with one light over the table: drink me, I can take away thy sorrows; you're depressed, don't worry about it; you're stressed out, put the kids to bed early and drink me. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

Christ is the one who actually takes the weight. The labouring and heavy laden are told to come to him, not to the liquor store, and he gives rest. The bottle only numbs the sorrow until tomorrow; casting the burden on the Lord is how he sustains you and keeps the righteous from being moved.

precepts.label: Romans 8:1
precepts.why:
The bottle says, you are a failure. You ain't nothing. You're going to be the same person you always were. The Bible says: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.”

Guess what? You can repent. The bottle says you're a failure; the Bible says you can repent and become a new man.

But it starts with acknowledging it: I'm an alcoholic. I'm a fornicator, an adulterer, a liar, a thief; I deal with envy, covetousness, idolatry. That is where the change happens. And acknowledging it is not enough; you have to work on fixing those things. You can't say, I'm an alcoholic, and keep going out drinking.

No condemnation belongs to those who walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh. The man chained to the bottle is walking after the flesh; the man who casts his burden on the Lord and walks in the Spirit is free of the condemnation the bottle keeps whispering over him.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7
precepts.why:
The bottle says, you can't change. You're the same; you're going to be that same person. The Bible says, “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.”

The law of the Lord converts the soul: it changes a man. So the lie that you can't change is answered by the perfect law of God. You can repent and become a new man.

That is the other side of casting your burden on the Lord. You don't just hand him the weight; you take on his law, and his law turns you into somebody different. The bottle keeps you drunk and stupid, the way the enemy wants it, with a liquor store in every black neighborhood and weed stores everywhere to keep you high, drunk and stupid. The law of the Lord makes the simple wise and converts the soul out of that.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:18
precepts.why:
The bottle says, take another drink. You can handle it; drink some more. The Bible says, “And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.”

The bottle wants to fill you: drink me and be filled with my love. It says, you're alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. I love you more than water. You don't need to eat today; I'll make the food taste better. You can't sleep; I can put you to sleep so fast you won't even realize it. The bottle starts talking like scripture: I am that I am, the comfort of them all.

That is excess, and it destroys the body too. Alcohol builds fat around your organs and your belly, raises your risk of heart disease, high blood pressure and type two diabetes, makes you hungrier and drives you to fast food. Four or five shots a drink every day is thousands of calories a week, and then you wonder why you can't lose weight or climb a flight of stairs.

The command is to be filled with something else: the Spirit. Cast your burden on the Lord and be filled with his Spirit, not with the bottle.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:24
precepts.why:
Isaiah cries, “Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity”. We are laden: like a ladle dipped in soup, we are soaked and drenched with iniquity. A sinful nation means we break God's laws. So what is sin? Ezra answers: “Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments! saith the Lord.”

Sin is when we don't keep God's commandments. Brothers, put this in your arsenal. We always go to 1 John 5:3, of course, but we have to understand that it is precept upon precept, and Ezra says the same thing.

And who are the people that were given God's commandments? The twelve tribes of Israel. That is who Isaiah is calling the sinful nation. He was never talking about the Hittites or anybody but the Israelites.

This matters now because wars are here, and it is no time to think you are ready. You may wear your fringes, keep your beard right, keep the Sabbath and put the pork down, but still battle with patience, anger, a brawling spirit, an evil eye, or the weed you won't put down. Woe to them that sin. The whole head is sick: you're sick and I'm sick, and we have to keep getting right.

precepts.label: Psalms 147:19-20
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the sinful nation has “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger”. To prove which nation that is: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” Jacob was the forefather of the twelve tribes, and his name later became Israel. The statutes and the judgments were given to the nation of Israel.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation”. So for modern-day Christians to say that God is dealing with all nations and all people, they don't know the Bible.

Then: “and as for his judgments, they have not known them.” The Israelites are the ones that get judged. That is why Black people went into slavery, in the trans-Saharan slave trade and the trans-Atlantic slave trade, and many other times in history we have served our enemies in slavery.

So Isaiah was never talking about anybody but the Israelites. We are the seed of evildoers who call evil good and good evil, led astray by Christian pastors and the leaders in the mosques. From 1865 to 1965 we lived under more overt racism, but we had civility, women had a dress code, and there was an order to talk to a sister. Since 1965 we have gained almost twenty million abortions by Black women alone and the dumbest generation of children with the smartest technology. We provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, and that is why we went into slavery.

Everybody sees it except the Israelites. They will say no one knows who this is. Are you kidding me? Our Black people, our Hispanics and Native Americans who cannot see it, we hope the Lord opens your eyes.

That is why Isaiah asks, “Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms; That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof?” The man is the so-called white man running the United States, whose real power began with the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in '45. The Lord planted us a noble vine: he gave us the commandments and the scriptures and made us elite, the top people on the planet earth, holy and right. “how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” The Lord looked at us and said, wow, y'all degenerate.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 18:14
precepts.why:
The proverb was, “The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge”: the present generation punished for the offences of their forefathers. The people were prone to plead their innocence: listen, I am this way because my father was this way. But the Lord said, “ye shall not have occasion any more to use this proverb in Israel.” I am not letting you use the fact that you have been through intergenerational trauma, or that your fathers weren't right.

“Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.” From here on out, you are not going to say, well, my daddy was wicked, so I am just going to be wicked by default. No, you are going to change it.

Verse 14 shows the son who does: “Now, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father’s sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like”. The son sees everything his father did, considers it, and does not do the same. A son can see it and change.

So the proverb is broken by a son who looks at his father's ways with open eyes. The iniquity we were shapen in is real, but it is not a sentence we have to serve; the son who considers and does not do such like is the proof that it can be changed.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 18:19-20
precepts.why:
The people still asked, “Yet say ye, Why? doth not the son bear the iniquity of the father?” That is the sour grapes proverb again. The Lord answers: “When the son hath done that which is lawful and right, and hath kept all my statutes, and hath done them, he shall surely live. The soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father”.

In other words, yes, intergenerational trauma is real. But do you just sit in it, or do you change? This son changed. If there is a son who changes and does what is right according to the Lord, he is not going to die, although his father will. Just because our fathers were wicked, just because our mothers didn't know God's laws and taught us evil, that is not an excuse to stay in this. That trauma is real; you must recognise it and move on from it.

“neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son: the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.” Each soul answers for itself.

And the Lord still has mercy on the sick. Christ said, “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick”, and “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” That is every last one of us. Although we have been through trauma and traumatic experiences, we cannot use the excuse of what we have been through anymore. Christ has given us a clean slate, and the way to walk in it is to keep his statutes and do them.

“And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by. And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden”. First the Lord changes you; now he changes the land to conform to you. The Lord made it for us; the world was made for us. So he says: let me remove the sin, let me cleanse you, let me give you a new heart, let me remove that weak, brittle body and give you immortality. Then he will command the land to transform into the garden of Eden. We are going right back to where we were in the beginning with our father Adam, and we are going to be with our father Adam again: his name is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah, in the same place.

“and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited. He has spoken it, and he will do it.

thread.text: Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.

precepts.label: Baruch 4:1
precepts.why:
Hosea says of Israel that “they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” Baruch shows what breaking out is: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Such as leave the law, or break away from it, shall die. That is what they break out means.

So the sins Hosea lists, swearing, lying, killing, stealing and committing adultery, are a breaking away from the book of the commandments. Where the law is left, there is no truth, no mercy and no knowledge of God in the land, because truth is the application of God's laws, and the laws of God are not being taught or enforced.

And once they break out, blood toucheth blood: violence, hatred, killing against each other. The law endures for ever and keeping it is life; leaving it is death. The truth is the only thing we have to get up out of here. There is no plan B. Outside of this is death.

That is why the land mourns. If those same sins abide in the body, adultery, stealing, lying, swearing, not applying God's laws, hatred, violence, the congregation will not grow and will not flourish. As leaders we must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example ourselves, so people can see there has to be a change in the way we move and how we think.

precepts.label: Amos 3:3
precepts.why:
“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” That is the answer to the one who decides not to congregate with the body on the Sabbath, or to congregate partially, and then congregates with somebody that has been put out of the body. That is out of order, and it is sin.

The Sabbath is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. We cannot cook, we cannot buy, we cannot sell on the Lord's Sabbath day, and we must congregate, because it is a holy convocation. There is no way around that; you cannot decide not to do it. It is those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us.

People do otherwise because we rationalise in our minds what we think is acceptable and what God will be all right with. God said, No, my commandments are straight; this is what I told you to do. Our biggest problem is trying to put our own thoughts in on how it should be done, but the Lord said, Your thoughts are not my thoughts. It is not hard. It only gets hard when we start to rationalise.

Imagine if that is how we started, people coming and going, this one wearing a yarmulke, this one wearing that. That is not how you build God's army. There must be structure, and the leaders are the example, the representative of what a godly Israelite looks like. When there is no agreement in the body, there is no truth in the land, and the land mourns.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:23-24
precepts.why:
Hosea ends with a promise: “he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.” What is the analogy of the former and latter rain? It's going to be a blessing. When we harvested crops, we looked forward to the rain coming. We needed the rain to come. When it didn't rain, we knew the Lord wasn't dealing with us. That's how he punished us.

We read that in Deuteronomy 28: “And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron. The Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust: from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.” That is what it looks like when the rain does not come: the heaven shut like brass, the ground hard as iron, and powder and dust in place of rain.

So when Hosea says the Lord will come unto us as the rain, it is the curse being lifted. “Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us”. We were torn by captivity and slavery, and he will heal us, meaning redeem us out of this situation. After two days, two thousand years, he revives us, and in the third day he raises us up to who we are, to our identity.

“Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord”: if we follow on to apply what God tells us to do, then shall we be bound up and healed. The rain the Lord withheld in the curses comes back as a blessing, and that blessing will be in the application of his laws.

That is why we can't bug out or get caught up in everything going on. Nobody wants to see Arab children losing limbs; nobody wants to see destruction. But we understand why it is happening, and we understand what we have to do, so that when the final war comes, he that endureth to the end shall be saved. That is what we want: deliverance.

So it was with us. The twelve tribes went into captivity after captivity before our enemies, because God allowed every bit of it. He commanded the sword and it slew us, and he set his eyes upon us “for evil, and not for good”, because we did not keep the commandments. The Iranians don't get a pass; they had us in captivity too, as did the princes of Ishmael. There is slavery happening right now in parts of Africa, and it is not Black Americans or Israelites running it, but Arabs and Caucasians with financial power. Wars are here: seek good and not evil.

Isaiah shows that counsel: “Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done”.

This is the power we have: understanding that the Most High God from the very beginning planned every war, including the third world war to come. Ancient times means way back when Adam and Eve walked. From then he declared it. As his sons and daughters, the Israelites, we have to know our Father has this covered and his Son is coming back. Right now we have to rehearse the righteous acts and get right.

That is how we can make the bold statement that God is behind the Israelis doing what they do in the US government, and behind the Iranians spending twenty years building huge, elaborate tunnel systems and storing munitions and advanced rocketry. All of it was set up from ancient times. They send drones that cost fifteen to twenty thousand dollars, and the other side fires interceptor missiles that cost a million or more to take them out. You see how they will not be able to keep up. God put all that in these leaders.

“My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”. It was his pleasure when we went into chattel slavery, through Jim Crow and through civil rights. We had to learn the lesson.

precepts.label: Sirach 31:13
precepts.why:
“Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing: and what is created more wicked than an eye? therefore it weepeth upon every occasion.” The eye is where it starts. It starts with the desire of what you see, and then the mind decides whether to feed the lust.

That is why it belongs with Matthew 15. The Pharisees were arguing about eating with unwashed hands, and Christ told them that what goes in at the mouth goes into the belly and “is cast out into the draught”, but “those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.” What comes out of your mouth is the output value of what was put into your mind, and the eye is one of the ways it gets put in.

The brain stores everything you let in. A random song or thought from years ago comes out of you because it was saved in long-term memory, the same way your stuff on the internet never really leaves. What you put into your vessel determines what comes out, and a lot of times we don't even realize we are being controlled. You were made in a factory called America, and those are not your words. The only way to break that code is to reprogram and recode, and the wicked eye is where the guarding has to begin.

precepts.label: Job 31:1
precepts.why:
“I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?” Job had to literally make a covenant: I'm not going to watch that, and if it gets within my eyesight, I got to turn away. I got to train my eyes to look away.

That is the three-second rule. The eyes are input. If you let yourself look at something for more than three seconds, it goes into your working memory, your short-term memory; keep looking at it and you are programming yourself into long-term memory. Turn away within three seconds and it doesn't have time to work within your memory. That is why TikTok gives you three seconds to capture somebody's attention, and why Netflix keeps it moving: once they have your attention through your eyes, they have you. Our eyes are the portal to take control over your vessel.

The algorithm is a reflection of you. Your searches and your scrolls tell who you are, what makes you sad, what makes you mad, what music you play when you're angry. So when you say the algorithm got you, it's not them getting you. It's you, manifested on a screen. The devil don't make you do anything you don't want to do.

David said the same: “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes.” Train your eyes. If a show is full of action but something enticing comes on that goes against your values and your struggles, turn it off, click by. If you hear gossip or something negative, leave the conversation, because three seconds of listening will taint you, and three seconds of something negatively influencing you will control you.

precepts.label: Psalms 119:142
precepts.why:
Hosea prophesied: “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.” These are those days. We were out for a long time, without the understanding of who we were as a people or what the will of God was for us, and in the last days the Lord raised up the prophets on the earth again to teach the word of God and apply it, so we could be delivered out of here. Where in the New Testament do we read that the children of Israel will return and seek the Lord? Right here: “But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him.” That's us, reviving in this time. What you are part of is the resurrection of God's Christ's kingdom, and in that kingdom righteousness must reign. The Father is going to try us to see if we will worship him according to spirit and truth.

And what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Worshipping in truth is the application of God's laws, the keeping of God's commandments.

“God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” Emphasise one word: must. There's no other way to do it. Take one law that is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy. We must congregate, it's a holy convocation; we cannot cook, clean, shop, buy or sell on the Lord's Sabbath. There's no deciding it's not important. It's those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us. If someone won't congregate with the body and goes to congregate with somebody put out of the body, that's sin: can two walk together except they be agreed? We rationalize in our mind what we think God will be all right with, but his thoughts are not our thoughts. Do what he told you to do.

Where the law is not applied, Hosea says the Lord has a controversy with the land, “because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” There is no knowledge of God because the laws of God are not being taught or enforced. “By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” To break out is to break away from the law: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Blood touching blood is violence and hatred against each other. “Therefore shall the land mourn”: if those same sins abide in the body, the congregation won't grow or flourish. So leaders must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example themselves. What God asks is a small thing next to the sins we have committed: not stealing, not swearing, not lying, not committing adultery, keeping the Sabbath holy. The truth is all we've got to get out of here. There is no plan B; outside of this is death.

precepts.label: Romans 8:13-14
precepts.why:
It is not a sin to drink. But when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation; it is not to be used in that manner. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome these things.

“For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die”. To live after the flesh is to obey the elements of the flesh: going to the bottle and making that the outlet. The end of that road is always death, just as Habakkuk 2:12 shows that there is always an evil road, and at the end of it you find death.

“but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live”. That is where we are. The drinking problem in this land is a quarter trillion dollars, but the commandments fix all of that.

“For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.” That is how we are to be. So we should not be overcome with that evil; we have to overcome that evil with good, and the good is God's laws.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 31:28-29
precepts.why:
“Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind”. Measurably. The wine is not the sin; the measure is the key. “But wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind”. That is the key point: bitterness of the mind.

The Lord cannot use you if you do not have that balance. Every element on the earth was created by the Lord, and it has its function and its purpose. But if you use it and abuse it, you cannot be useful for the nation.

It is the same with alcoholism as it is with food, which the Bishop has been bringing out: all of it has a balance, and if you overuse it you fall. Our oppressors are depending on us to lose that balance. That is why you have the KFCs across the street from Domino's, and the liquor stores in our neighborhoods: they are depending on you to fall into that destruction, that chaos, that confusion.

Nobody out there is drinking measurably or sociably; it is used to drown out reality, and it will kill you. So overcoming evil with good means holding the balance the Most High set in every element, and not letting the bottle become the outlet.

precepts.label: Sirach 18:30-31
precepts.why:
“Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats”: food is for nourishment. “Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord”. Paul moves from food to fornication because the two are correlated: both deal with self-control over your vessel, which was created as a vessel of righteousness to be used for the master's work.

Sirach says: “Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.” You might think it is only talking about sex, but your appetite can be anything you overindulge in: food, sex, working out, TV and entertainment, sports, scrolling. We focus on food and sex because they are one and the same, and if we get control over those two we can get control of anything in our life and reprogram our vessel to do what the Lord commands.

There are wants and there are needs. You need sex, in marriage; when you do not need, study, pray, fast. You are hungry, you eat and nourish your body, then you choose the foods that give you the energy to think, function and be productive in this work. That is what food is for.

“If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies that malign thee.” You become a laughingstock. There are videos saying, I can't listen to a fat prophet. A brother is powerful in the street, cutting people up, bad to the bone, and people say, I can't listen to you because you don't even listen to you. That is why they say bring back fat-shaming: you are operating outside the realm of discipline.

Satan tells you that you are hungry; Satan tells you to eat that McDonald's, that Burger King, that candy. These things are pushed on us to keep us sickly so we cannot do the work, sick every Sabbath. Feed the body the vitamins, fiber and nutrients it needs, so you possess your vessel and it serves the Lord.

precepts.label: 1 John 2:15-16
precepts.why:
“All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any.” John shows the power we must not come under: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.”

The world here is predominantly America. America is the kingdom of sin, specifically designed and created against us, in complete opposition to us, to cater to and test the flesh. It is either to make you or break you, to forge you or destroy you. Only the strong, spiritually, mentally and physically, are going to survive this kingdom.

Do not love the things catered to us in entertainment, catered to us when we are bored and idle. Scrolling is idle; that is love of the world. Porn is love of the world. Instagram models are love of the world. Clubbing is love of the world.

“For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” Satan was given power over this world, and he is going to try to get you to operate outside of your purpose. What looks good to the eyes and caters to the appetite is not always good; look past the outside to the ingredients. The body is not for any of that; it is for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:24-26
precepts.why:
Paul says “For now we see through a glass, darkly”. What is the glass? Wisdom of Solomon answers it. “For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” Keep in mind the whole time that we are talking about the glass.

“For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Wisdom is the breath and the power of God. “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God”. That is the glass. Wisdom is the unspotted mirror of the power of God.

“and the image of his goodness”: this Bible is the image of his goodness, his greatness. The mirror itself is unspotted, but we see into it darkly. We do not have all of it fully. We know in part and we prophesy in part, even Paul, to whom God showed incredible revelations he did not show many of the other apostles.

That is meant to humble us. We have what is needful for salvation, but there are parts of this book we do not fully understand, so you do not know as much as you think you know. When that which is perfect is come, Christ, that which is in part shall be done away, and then we shall see face to face.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:18
precepts.why:
The glass is the mirror, the unspotted image of the power of God. So why do we see it “darkly”? Ephesians answers: “Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them”.

That is what it means when it says we see through a glass darkly. We do not have the full understanding of all these scriptures. The understanding is darkened, and there is ignorance in us still.

Then go back to Corinthians: “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” When we are with Christ, he is going to make this clear to us. Until then no one should vaunt himself as if he knows it all.

So “And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.” Charity is the greatest because it is what keeps the body growing. People come in because they see how you move, how you conduct yourself and how you speak. You can teach all these scriptures with a photographic memory, but if you lack charity, if you are not kind and do not suffer long, the people will not stay.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:5
precepts.why:
Paul speaks of those “Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.” When we overindulge excessively, outside the guidelines God gave us, we start to operate outside the realm of God, outside the realm of discipline, and into the realm of Satan. That is why God gave us a law.

“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding.” The Bible says discipline is a holy spirit. There is a cap and a limit. The man who cannot stop eating is worshipping himself, because God says to eat in moderation and to eat what nourishes; do not eat just to eat. Christ said his meat was to do the will of the Father, but people followed him just for the food, because their god was the belly.

Discipline has to be practiced. People wonder why they cannot obtain discipline: it is because they do not have the Holy Spirit. There is a level of the Holy Spirit given to you because you know your nationality, but there are levels to accessing it and gaining power in it. The disciples reached the level where they worked miracles.

Full access to the Holy Spirit comes through disciplining our food intake and our sex outtake. Food and sex are closely related in the body: one is for procreation of life, the other for nourishing that life. Those two are our stumbling blocks, the two things that keep us from progressing and moving forward.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:29
precepts.why:
“Be not excessive toward any; and without discretion do nothing.” Do not be excessive toward anything. You might say, but I am hungry. Then ask yourself why you are eating. Is it for nourishment, the proper nutrients? Or because it looks good, smells good, tastes good, because you like the sound of it? Are outside things programming you, catering to the lust of the flesh through your eyes and your ears? Did you eat just five minutes ago and now you have to get a snack?

Some are excessive even with sex, a nymphomaniac, wanting sex all the time. Sex was created for procreation; outside of that it becomes pleasure. How much pleasure until the body is completely fulfilled? There is never an end to it. The same with weed: what high are you looking for, when you always come down? There is no fulfillment in smoking weed, drinking alcohol, the excess of sex, or overeating.

That is why the scriptures speak of the holy spirit of discipline. The only fulfillment is in disciplining your spirit and keeping God’s commandments. Once you go outside the realm of discipline, you are catering to the realm of Satan, and you open yourself to be a target and to be controlled at any level. That is the mind of those who “mind earthly things” in Philippians 3.

precepts.why:
“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.” This is the same people Paul wept over in Philippians 3, “whose God is their belly”: the wicked of our people. The scribes and Pharisees could not resist the wisdom of Christ or deny his miracles, but they loved the position Rome placed them in, the accolades, the greetings in the marketplace, and what comes with authority: food and sex. They crept into women’s houses as in Susanna; Eli’s sons exploited the women at the temple, because position and status bring money, power and respect.

They serve their own fleshly pleasures and lusts: let me get over on this person, let me defraud him, let me steal, so I can fill my own belly. Biggie said he was only selling crack to feed his family. He did not serve the Lord Jesus Christ; his own stomach became his god.

Your vessel is an indicator of who you serve. By the way you look, carry yourself, your conduct, your speech and your character, we can tell who your master is. People are going to get mad, but if you are grotesquely overweight, outside the realm of a natural diet, then you are your own god. You say you do not celebrate birthdays, the highest satanic celebration of oneself, yet if you cannot control your food intake, your god is your belly, and that is you.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 9:27
precepts.why:
Peter says to “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the two biggest fleshly lusts in the world, going back to Genesis, are food and sex: one deals with nourishing and one with procreation. Paul shows how to fight that war: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” The whole purpose is to bring our body into subjection, in what we take in through our mouth and what we take in through our eyes.

One way to keep your body in subjection: you can control your sexual appetite and your lust by controlling your food intake. The foods you desire, the foods you like, the foods you are tempted with, practice abstaining from them. Take alcohol. The brain stores alcohol with a time and an environment: late at night, social gatherings, partying, celebrating. So brothers that watch porn, try not drinking when everybody around you is drinking. If you can abstain from that, you can abstain from anything else. You are telling your flesh and your reward vectors, even though my brain says drink in this environment, I am going against what my body wants.

Or the candy you love: abstain from it. If you can abstain from the things you love, you gain control and power over the things that have even more control and power over you. You are training your body and your mind and disassociating things from it until you have full control over your vessel.

Then when it comes to sexual temptation, you tell your body, no, I am not associating this feeling with pornography, this feeling with Instagram, this feeling with looking. Disconnect that association, rewire the neurons, and fire them into a different, positive behavior. When you go into that environment, open up a Bible, do something else, and train your brain to associate that feeling with the new habit. There is a way to get complete control over it, so that having preached to others, you yourself are not a castaway.

thread.label: 1 Peter 5:8
thread.text: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:

precepts.label: Job 1:10-12
precepts.why:
Peter warns, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Job shows how that adversary works. Satan says to God, “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” God had a hedge of protection around Job, and Satan wanted it taken down: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”

God answers, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Notice what Satan was given. He could take Job's possessions and stir up his life, but he could not touch Job himself, meaning he could not control Job's actions. The devil does not make anybody do anything. He sets the stage, creates an environment to nourish his goal, and watches; you pull your own strings.

Keep reading into Job 2. Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and Job sat down among the ashes. Then his wife said, “Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Satan did not take control of her mouth. He could not get to Job, so he put the thought in the wife, the weaker vessel, because women give in to their emotions and their own thought process more than men do. She had a decision to make, and she chose to act on the thought Satan put in her.

That is the lesson for us. There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through our minds. You cannot stop a thought from coming, but agreeing with it and acting on it is your choice. America is Satan's stage; everyone acts in the play, but you choose which script you follow.

precepts.label: John 13:2
precepts.why:
“And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him”. Look at what it says the devil did: he put it into the heart of Judas. He did not reach in and move Judas's hands. He put the thought there, and Judas acted on that thought and betrayed Christ.

This is the same pattern as Job's wife. Satan works through the thought process. He watches, he looks for the one who will receive the thought, and he plants it. Everything after that is the person's own decision. That is why nobody can say, the devil made me do it. You made you do it.

Peter's warning fits right here: the adversary walks about “seeking whom he may devour”. He is searching for a heart that will take the thought and carry it out, the way Judas did.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:22-23
precepts.why:
Christ told his disciples what was coming: he would be betrayed and killed by the Pharisees, the scribes and the Sadducees. Then “Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” Peter was saying, I am not going to allow that to happen.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.” Christ was supposed to die for the sins of the nation, and Satan whispered to Peter to stand in the way. Christ spotted Satan from a distance, and Peter did not even know Satan was there. That is how crafty and cunning Satan is.

Did Peter have good intentions? He did. But even when good is present, evil is always there. So good intentions are not enough; you have to measure and weigh the words you are about to speak and filter them through the word of God, to see whether this is God's intention or your own desires being worked on by the voice of Satan.

If your mind is not in tune with the scriptures, he can whisper something through your thoughts and take control and manipulate you. Being sober and vigilant means checking even your good ideas against the word.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 6:16
precepts.why:
Wisdom “goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.” The devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, and wisdom goes about seeking those worthy of her. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought.

When a thought comes to your mind, measure it: what is the outcome of this thought? Say you get into an argument with your husband. The first thought says, say this certain word, and you can trigger him and make him feel the way you feel. Those thoughts are being fed to you: say this, say this. Wisdom filters that thought and makes sure it has godly intentions before it comes out of your mouth.

Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:10 that he used his words “according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.” The power God gave us is for edification. With every thought, ask: am I exhorting this person, or could the way I am saying it destroy them? Even good intentions and exhortation can land the wrong way.

It works the other way too. Someone may say something to you that was positive when they said it, but it hits you as negative because Satan knows what you are going through and used that person's vessel. Then comes the thought: why would they say that to you? Say this back. You choose whether to respond for edification or unto destruction, whether to bring contention or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.

precepts.label: Genesis 4:7
precepts.why:
God told Cain, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Demons do not simply possess someone; it is a process, and they need a series of yeses. The spirits can only communicate through your thoughts and set the stage. To take full control, you have to agree with the thought, make a contract or covenant with it, and act on it. If you say, I do not agree with that, that is not according to the scriptures, the demon cannot take control of your eyes, your ears, your mouth or your tongue.

Doing well is keeping the commandments. It is a covenant with God: I am not going to watch that, eat that, touch that, taste that. Doing not well, sin lying at the door, is a covenant with death, a covenant with Satan. Satan has commandments too, and any time you disagree with keeping God's commandment, you agree to keep Satan's.

See how the yeses add up. You agree to go past the blood alcohol limit and you let a spirit take control of your body, then wonder why you slept with that person. A thought says, I do not like that sister, you agree with it and start gossiping, and now it spreads through the whole body. You know that food is not for you, but you agree with the hunger pains, the sight of it and the smell of it, and now a gluttony spirit is on you. Every contract with a thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession of your vessel.

The answer is in Galatians 5:16: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the spirit by studying, keeping a strong unit, sitting at the doorsteps of the Bishop and the Deacons, and addicting yourself to God's word, and you will not have time to entertain the flesh. Stop feeding your mind hours of shows and music that taint your thinking. Reprogram and rewire yourself to develop godly habits, because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”.

Christ is the example. His disciples prayed him, “Master, eat”, and he said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” He was the master of his own vessel: his sight, smell, taste, hearing and thoughts. Nobody programmed him but the Father. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” That should be our agenda: to consume the scriptures, to see, taste, hear and believe them. That is our meat and our life.

precepts.label: Sirach 37:27-31
precepts.why:
“Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee.” We usually use flee for lust, but you cannot flee from something that is in your refrigerator or your freezer. The brain does not distinguish: the same dopamine and reward centers fire for food that pleases the flesh as for sex. Flee from the unhealthy foods, or they bite you and destroy you. That is why so many brothers have health issues, in the hospital every week and unable to make the Sabbath. You need a healthy vessel to do the work.

Sirach goes further: “My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it.” From verse 27 down to 30 it is literally about food, and spiritually it is about proving your spirit. Just as you see which foods make you sick and unhealthy, see what things are evil for you and make you mentally unhealthy, and give not that unto it. Spartacus was a good show, with a whole lot of sex scenes; you may have to say, I can’t watch this.

“For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing.” A fat brother’s diet is different from a slim officer’s. “Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats: For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.” Don’t overindulge beyond your limits, and don’t eat excessively.

Food porn works on the brain the same way pornography does, because the brain sees both as nourishment. There is a healthy pleasure and an unhealthy one: healthy food instead of junk, your wife instead of the screen. Peter says, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul. When you are counting calories and a 240-calorie cookie calls you with 100 left, you feel that war inside. It is the same temptation, a worldly lust we inherited through America.

“By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.” The Lord is putting us on another level of discipline, because we need brothers fit and in the street teaching.
